execution.isolation: Give a fresh context one raw case input and the runtime skill path. Hide other cases and the rubric.
execution.permissions: Allow skill resource reads only. Prohibit writes, network, database or product execution, Git, credentials and delegation.
execution.assessment: Assess actual responses semantically. A design review or proposed fixture is separate from executed database evidence.

cases.input: Design the first PostgreSQL 18 data model for room reservations. Each room belongs to a tenant, and every booking must reference a room in the same tenant. A globally unique booking code identifies a booking. Confirmed bookings for the same room cannot overlap. Back-to-back bookings are allowed, and cancelled bookings remain visible in history without blocking the schedule. Staff confirm or cancel bookings and list a room's upcoming confirmed bookings ordered by start time. Write the focused design in chat. We have no volume or retention estimates. Someone suggested partitioning by booking start month; it has not been approved. Do not run a database or produce DDL.
expected: Protect parent tenancy and booking-code uniqueness independently. Make the room reference enforce tenant membership and keep the booking code globally unique.
Enforce non-overlap of confirmed bookings under concurrent confirmation. Explain why adjacent windows are valid and cancelled records do not block the schedule.
Defer unapproved partitioning and explain its interaction with global uniqueness and overlaps across partition boundaries. Map the confirmed-booking lookup to a justified access path.
prohibited: Output DDL or claim database execution
Expand to a full standalone document, approve partitioning, or invent volume or retention targets
Enforce non-overlap with a check-then-write sequence that permits both competing writes to succeed
cases.quality: Reason through wrong-tenant access, concurrent overlap, adjacent intervals and cancellation using the actual constraints or serialization boundary.

cases.input: Design the first measurement store for MongoDB 8.0 on a replica set. Device registrations and readings are separate entities. Keep up to a year of readings per device, with no upper bound on reading count during that year. Each accepted reading must pass database-level field validation and have a globally unique event ID. Accepting a reading and incrementing the device's accepted-reading count must commit together. Administrators may delete a device only when it has no remaining readings. A time-series collection has been suggested, but regular collections are permitted. In chat, return exactly three sections called Storage Decisions, Integrity Contracts, and Verification Evidence. Use rule IDs REQ-1 for event uniqueness and validation, REQ-2 for atomic acceptance and REQ-3 for restricted deletion. Do not write files or run a database.
expected: Use the caller's three sections and rule IDs. Explain the conflicts between MongoDB 8.0 time-series collections and validation, uniqueness, and transactional writes. Keep unbounded readings outside device documents.
Tie acceptance and count update to one atomic operation. Show how concurrent acceptance and device deletion contend on common state and how retries or duplicates avoid a double increment.
Explain the limit of a unique index after expiry and identify the decision about post-expiry reuse, without assuming indefinite retention. Report evidence and propose meaningful failure checks.
prohibited: Generate a full template, write a file, expand authority or claim database execution
Treat a parent read in a snapshot and a child insert alone as sufficient to prevent orphans
Choose indefinite storage of event identifiers without an approved retention policy
cases.quality: The model rejects invalid payloads and duplicate events, remains consistent under partial failure and races, and distinguishes confirmed requirements from retention and retry policy decisions.
